newsitem.title: USA: San Diego mayor vows early vote on stadium plan.
newsitem.headline: San Diego mayor vows early vote on stadium plan.

text.p: A special election on San Diego's plan to expand Jack Murphy Stadium should be held as soon as possible, city officials said on Thursday.

Mayor Susan Golding and several city council members vowed to put the issue to the voters quickly, after the city's clerk announced that petitions seeking a public referendum on the expansion were valid.
According to a petition review by local election officials, almost 47,000 of the 59,000 petition signatures submitted were valid. Petitioners needed about 28,000.
To be sure, the petition review did not settle the dispute between city officials and critics of the expansion plan.
The city agreed to a $60 million plan in 1995 to expand the stadium to 70,000 seats. But in December, the city amended the contract, adding $18 million to the project.
Golding will seek to place the $18 million amendment to the expansion plan on the city ballot "as quickly as legally possible," her spokeswoman said.

Attorneys for project opponents maintain that the $18 million addition substantially changed the original agreement. As a result, the entire expansion project should be placed on the ballot, attorney Mike Aguirre said.
A hearing was set for January 29 in superior court on whether the referendum should apply to the entire project or just to the $18 million added on last month.
City officials said a special election on the expansion plan could be held as early as May.
